## The SDR Paradox: High Volume, High Turnover

Sales Development Representatives are the engine of B2B revenue growth. They are also the role with the highest turnover in most organizations — averaging 35% annually, with a median tenure of just 14.2 months. This creates a perpetual hiring cycle that drains resources and destabilizes pipelines.

This guide provides a scalable framework for hiring SDRs that reduces attrition, accelerates ramp time, and delivers predictable pipeline generation.

### The Unit Economics of SDR Hiring

Before scaling, understand the math:

- Average cost to hire an SDR : $4,200 (sourcing, interviewing, onboarding)
- Average ramp time : 3.2 months to full productivity
- Fully loaded cost during ramp : $18,000-$25,000 (salary + benefits + training + management time)
- Average annual pipeline generated per SDR : $1.2M-$2.4M (varies by ACV)
- Breakeven point : Month 5-7 for most organizations

When an SDR leaves at month 10, you have captured only 3-5 months of productive output after a 5-month investment. This is why retention is not a "nice to have" — it is the most important variable in your SDR economics.

### Defining the Ideal SDR Profile

The highest-performing SDR teams hire for traits, not experience:

Must-have traits:

- Coachability — willingness to take feedback and iterate quickly
- Resilience — ability to handle 50+ rejections daily without losing energy
- Curiosity — genuine interest in understanding prospect businesses
- Competitive drive — internal motivation to hit and exceed targets
- Communication clarity — ability to articulate value in 30 seconds

Nice-to-have experience:

- Prior sales or customer-facing roles (retail, hospitality, call centers)
- Familiarity with CRM tools (Salesforce, HubSpot)
- Understanding of the target industry

Overrated qualifications:

- Specific degree requirements (business, marketing)
- Prior SDR experience at a competitor (often comes with bad habits)
- Years of experience (diminishing returns beyond 1 year in SDR roles)

### Sourcing at Scale

Hiring 5-10 SDRs per quarter requires multiple active channels:

- University partnerships : Build relationships with business, communications, and liberal arts programs. SDRs from non-traditional backgrounds (philosophy, psychology, theater) often outperform business majors.
- Bootcamp and career changer pipelines : Sales bootcamp graduates come pre-trained on fundamentals. They are motivated and have self-selected into the profession.
- Internal referrals : Top SDRs know other high performers. Offer $2,000-$5,000 referral bonuses — well below the cost of a bad hire.
- Subscription sourcing : TaaS delivers pre-screened SDR candidates weekly, scored on coachability, communication, and drive. See pricing for volume hiring plans.
- LinkedIn and job boards : Cast a wide net but use structured screening to manage volume.

### The Interview Process That Predicts Success

SDR interviews should be practical, not theoretical:

Stage 1: Phone Screen (20 minutes)

Evaluate communication quality, energy, and basic research (did they prepare?). Ask:

- "What do you know about our company and who we sell to?"
- "Walk me through a time you had to persuade someone who initially said no."

Stage 2: Role Play (30 minutes)

Simulate a cold call. Provide a brief company description and prospect persona. Evaluate:

- Active listening and question-asking

- Energy and enthusiasm under pressure

This single exercise is the strongest predictor of SDR success. Candidates who perform well here are 3x more likely to hit quota in month 4.

Stage 3: Manager Interview (30 minutes)

Assess coachability and cultural fit:

- Give feedback on the role play and ask the candidate to redo it. Coachable candidates improve immediately.
- Discuss career goals — SDRs who see the role as a stepping stone to account executive or customer success stay longer.
- Explore work style and team dynamics preferences.

### Compensation Models That Drive Performance

The right comp plan aligns SDR behavior with business outcomes:

| Component | Range | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Base salary | $45K-$65K | Market competitiveness and financial security |
| Variable (OTE) | $20K-$40K | Performance incentive |
| Accelerators | 1.5-2x above quota | Reward top performers disproportionately |
| SPIFs | $200-$1,000/month | Short-term behavior drivers |

OTE split : 65/35 (base/variable) for new SDRs, moving to 55/45 as they ramp. Avoid splits more aggressive than 50/50 — they increase anxiety and turnover without improving performance.

Quota design : Set achievable quotas that 60-70% of SDRs hit. If fewer than 50% are hitting quota, the problem is the quota, not the people.

### The 90-Day Ramp Playbook

Structured ramp programs reduce time-to-productivity by 40%:

Week 1-2: Foundation

- Product training and certification
- ICP and persona deep-dive
- CRM and tools onboarding
- Shadow 10+ calls with top performers

Week 3-4: Guided Practice

- Make first calls with manager listening
- Daily role-play sessions (15 minutes)
- Begin email outreach with reviewed templates
- First pipeline meetings (observe, then participate)

Month 2: Ramp Quota

- 50% of full quota target
- Weekly 1:1s with manager (coaching focus)
- Peer learning sessions
- First independent meetings booked

Month 3: Full Production

- 75-100% of full quota
- Bi-weekly 1:1s
- Begin mentoring newer SDRs
- Career path discussion with manager

### Reducing Attrition: The Retention Playbook

The three biggest drivers of SDR attrition are:

- No clear career path (cited by 47% of departing SDRs)
- Inadequate coaching (cited by 38%)
- Compensation dissatisfaction (cited by 31%)

Address each systematically:

- Career pathing : Define explicit promotion criteria to AE, customer success , or sales enablement. Publish timelines (12-18 months typical). Celebrate promotions publicly.
- Coaching investment : Sales managers should spend 40% of their time coaching, not just inspecting metrics. Train managers on coaching methodologies.
- Compensation reviews : Benchmark quarterly against market data. Adjust base salaries annually. Add non-monetary benefits (learning budgets, conference attendance, flexible work).

### Scaling Beyond 20 SDRs

At scale, new challenges emerge:

- Quality control : Implement call recording and scoring. Use AI-powered conversation intelligence tools to identify coaching opportunities at scale.
- Manager ratio : Maintain 6-8 SDRs per frontline manager. Beyond this, coaching quality degrades.
- Segmentation : Divide SDRs by market segment (enterprise vs. SMB), geography, or product line for deeper expertise.
- Enablement team : Once you have 20+ SDRs, a dedicated sales enablement function (content, training, tools) pays for itself within one quarter.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How many SDRs should I hire at once?

Hire in cohorts of 3-5 for optimal training and peer support. Cohorts create healthy competition and shared learning. Avoid hiring more SDRs than your managers can effectively coach (6-8 per manager).

### What is the ideal SDR-to-AE ratio?

The industry standard is 2-3 SDRs per AE, but this varies by deal size. For enterprise sales ($100K+ ACV), 1:1 is common. For SMB ($10K-$30K ACV), 3:1 or 4:1 can work. Optimize based on pipeline velocity, not headcount ratios.

### Should SDRs report to sales or marketing?

SDRs should report to sales. When SDRs report to marketing, there is often a disconnect between pipeline quality and sales team expectations. The manager should be a former SDR or AE who understands the daily reality of the role.

### How do I measure SDR quality, not just activity?

Track qualified opportunity creation rate, not just meetings booked. A great SDR books fewer meetings of higher quality. Key metrics: SQL conversion rate, average deal size of sourced opportunities, and pipeline-to-close ratio.
